original_text: TWO CLASSES OF CORE CHANGE, recorded in ARCHITECTURE.md because 'core change' had been read as 'another 15-hour run' when most are nothing of the kind. Changes that alter the filter's NUMERICS (the fuel-burn fix, a prior, a measurement model, the step loop) invalidate existing runs and a re-run is the price. Changes DOWNSTREAM of the filter (terminal.rs, impacts.rs, crates/hypothesis, ImpactView, config keys that select a module) do not change what the filter computes; `make regress` proves it by returning byte-identical base output against main, existing runs stay valid, and the development loop is `mh370 terminal <run-dir> <config> <out-dir>`, a stage-2-only sweep off a stored hand-off. All end-of-flight core requests are in the second class, and `make regress` is the gate - if it fails, something in the step loop was touched that should not have been.
